newsitem.title: USA: TransTexas in talks to sell Lobo unit.
newsitem.headline: TransTexas in talks to sell Lobo unit.

text.p: TransTexas Gas Corp on Wednesday said it was in talks to sell its TransTexas Transmission Corp unit for more than $1.1 billion in cash.
The unit owns the Lobo Trend natural gas properties and a 1,100 mile pipeline. TransTexas declined to detail the talks, but said they were with an unaffiliated third party.
"This is the highest priority for the company at this time and we are endeavoring to close (the deal) as quickly as possible," said President and Chief Operating Officer Arnold Brackenridge.
Brackenridge said that using the proceeds in the Bob West North natural gas field and elsewhere would outweigh the benefits of further investment in Lobo Trend.
TransTexas Gas stock jumped to a year-high of $17-1/2 on the news, then settled at 17-1/4, up $1 by 1015 EST/1515 GMT.

"Assuming that a transaction can be concluded at a price beneficial to the company, it makes sense to monetize this subsidiary now and focus on the ongoing growth of our new development areas," Brackenridge said.
TransTexas Gas is the third largest gas producer in Texas with gross production capacity of 800 million cubic feet equivalent.

Lobo Trend, which had accounted for the bulk of TransTexas Gas's production until 1996, now accounts for less than half since the discovery of Bob West North and other fields. ((-- New York Newsrom 212 859 1610))
